name: Shudder to Think
label: Dischord
lede: A glam falsetto in a straight-edge town, an MTV Buzz Clip nobody saw coming, a run of film scores, and, twenty-seven years later, a new single back on Dischord.

eras.title: A hardcore band that shuddered to think
eras.text: Shudder to Think began as a teenage hardcore band and turned into something D.C. hadn't heard: punk played like theater, with a singer who went for falsetto instead of a bark. Dischord calls them part of a younger wave that grew up on the scene without copying it.

years.h: Shudder to Think starts as Stüge
years.p: Bassist Stuart Hill and drummer [[Mike Russell|5052af59-8df4-485a-89ff-d34cd5314b0d]] form Stüge, a hardcore band, with guitarist Sam Fleming and singer Bobby Jones.

years.h: Stüge finds singer Craig Wedren in a school play
years.p: Sam Fleming and Bobby Jones leave for college. Stuart Hill brings in guitarist [[Chris Matthews|824d9e26-0d6b-4ec7-b7af-78505ed771b0]] from the new wave band 3-2-1, and Matthews suggests [[Craig Wedren|2da87294-e651-420b-8d25-2dbc3b29a285]], whom he'd seen perform in a school play.

years.h: Mike Russell names Shudder to Think on a car ride
years.p: Driving to practice, drummer Mike Russell says he shudders to think they'd end up just another hardcore band. The phrase becomes the band's name, and the music starts drifting toward post-hardcore.

years.h: Curses, Spells, Voodoo, Mooses · Sammich
years.p: Shudder to Think's debut album, on the small Sammich label rather than Dischord.

eras.title: Glam in a straight-edge town
eras.text: On Dischord, Shudder to Think were the odd band out: melodic, theatrical and a little strange, on a label known for fury. By 1992 half the band had changed, with Nathan Larson arriving from Swiz and Adam Wade from Jawbox.

years.h: Ten Spot · Dischord No. 46
years.p: Shudder to Think's first record for Dischord. The band had already appeared on Dischord's State of the Union compilation.

years.h: Funeral at the Movies · Dischord No. 54
years.p: Shudder to Think's second Dischord record, later paired with Ten Spot on one release (No. 55).

years.h: Chris Matthews plays his last Shudder to Think show
years.p: Guitarist Chris Matthews leaves for school. [[Nathan Larson|c0845dd8-ef14-486c-92b6-260727732b4c]], who had played bass in [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]], takes the guitar slot.
years.xp: Nathan Larson came over from [[Swiz|eea2f3d8-1e94-436c-ae66-4633f99f55be]], where he'd played bass, and switched to guitar. Within six months drummer Mike Russell left too, leaving Craig Wedren and Stuart Hill as the only members from the 1980s records.

years.h: Shudder to Think recorded live in Albig, Germany
years.p: A show on Shudder to Think's German tour becomes Your Choice Live Series Vol. 21, released by Tobby Holzinger's Your Choice label.

years.h: Mike Russell leaves; Jawbox's Adam Wade takes the drums
years.p: Mike Russell, Shudder to Think's drummer since the Stüge days, plays his last show. [[Adam Wade|d2502278-bf42-445b-98a2-9249af4c8a0a]], just out of [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]], takes over.

years.h: Get Your Goat · Dischord No. 67
years.p: Shudder to Think's last album for Dischord before their move to Epic, a major label.

eras.title: Buzz Bin, of all places
eras.text: Touring with Fugazi and The Smashing Pumpkins put Shudder to Think in front of far bigger crowds, and Epic came calling. They signed, becoming, by Dischord's count, one of only two bands ever to leave the label for a major.

years.h: Shudder to Think tour with Fugazi and the Smashing Pumpkins
years.p: Two very different tours in one year: with Fugazi, the D.C. flagship, and with the Smashing Pumpkins, a Chicago band on its way to arenas.

q: We wanted our music to reach the most people and make a living.
years.h: Shudder to Think leave Dischord for Epic
years.p: Shudder to Think sign to Epic, championed by A&R man Michael Goldstone, and move to New York. [[Jawbox|016fba14-1fc6-4986-86c2-2113ec9b28de]] were the only other Dischord band to make the jump.
years.xp:
Craig Wedren has said the reason was simple: they wanted to be heard by as many people as possible and to make a living at it. Looking back, the band has described Epic as supportive throughout.

Not every fan agreed. Wedren told PopMatters that one fan picketed a Shudder to Think show while they were opening for [[The Smashing Pumpkins|ba0d6274-db14-4ef5-b28d-657ebde1a396]], in defense of Dischord.

years.h: Pony Express Record · Epic
years.p: Shudder to Think's Epic debut, produced by [[Ted Niceley|fbe203ef-a327-4d7e-af16-a10d55b7347d]] on analog tape in a big room for what the band called a widescreen sound. Angular, mathematical and nothing like its alt-rock shelf-mates.
years.xp: The drums were locked to a click the band nicknamed the Russian Dragon. Per Wikipedia, the album had sold 30,000 copies in the U.S. by late October 1994, and 60,000 by February 1997.

years.cap: Craig Wedren live with Shudder to Think, 1994 · Wikimedia
q: I worshipped them. There was one year I saw them twelve times.
years.h: Shudder to Think's X-French Tee Shirt becomes an MTV Buzz Clip
years.p: The X-French Tee Shirt video becomes an MTV Buzz Clip, and the single reaches No. 36 on the Radio & Records alternative chart. For a record as strange as Pony Express Record, a small miracle.
years.xp: PopMatters' look back dates the Buzz Bin run to spring 1995 and says Rolling Stone held it up as a sign the Buzz Bin had run its course. The song outlived the argument: [[Deftones|7527f6c2-d762-4b88-b5e2-9244f1e34c46]] would cover bits of it live, and [[Incubus|e3e0abcd-7671-4482-a9d8-462f5acc9be5]] played part of it at Lollapalooza 2003.

years.h: Craig Wedren is diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma
years.p: Shortly after promotion for Pony Express Record began, Craig Wedren, then 26, was diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma, he told Vanyaland in 2025. His doctor said it was curable, and Wikipedia says he beat it over the next few years.
years.xp: Wedren has said that at that age he didn't really grasp what the diagnosis meant. The band kept going, but its next album, 50,000 B.C., didn't land, and by 1998 the energy had moved to film scores.

years.h: [[Jeff Buckley|e6e879c0-3d56-4f12-b3c5-3ce459661a8e]] names Shudder to Think a favorite
years.p: In a 1995 interview, Jeff Buckley counts Shudder to Think among the bands he loves, and [[James Iha|a89811cc-4514-48b2-b353-dba9debf7055]] of the Smashing Pumpkins calls them a wholly original rock band.
years.xp: The same year Epic released So Into You as a single.

eras.title: From the stage to the screen
eras.text: 50,000 B.C., the second Epic album, missed, and the band's energy moved toward film. In 1998 they had songs across three movies and an invitation from Pearl Jam, and then, when Nathan Larson left, no band.

years.h: Adam Wade out, [[Kevin March|5f5f1eb3-c441-4758-b5a0-8873f098735e]] in on drums
years.p: Kevin March, drummer of [[The Dambuilders|baf6c035-1e22-4a4c-ad4b-ea294fd41a1b]], replaces Adam Wade in Shudder to Think.
Shudder to Think's second and last album for Epic gets mixed reviews and is, in Wikipedia's words, a commercial flop.

years.h: Shudder to Think score three films in one year
years.p: Shudder to Think score High Art and First Love, Last Rites and land two songs in Todd Haynes' glam-rock film Velvet Goldmine. It's the road both Craig Wedren and Nathan Larson will follow for decades.
years.xp:
High Art came out on Velvel and First Love, Last Rites on Epic's soundtrack arm. The Velvet Goldmine songs sat alongside the film's glam covers and originals.

After the band stopped, the film work became both men's day job: Wedren on David Wain's projects from The State circle, including Wet Hot American Summer and Reno 911!, and Larson on scores and his band Hot One.

years.h: Shudder to Think open for [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]] in Australia
years.p: Pearl Jam invite Shudder to Think on their Australian tour and slip a snippet of the Shudder song Pebbles into their own set.

years.h: Nathan Larson leaves, and Shudder to Think end
years.p: With Nathan Larson gone, Shudder to Think stop. Craig Wedren goes on to score Wet Hot American Summer, School of Rock and later Yellowjackets; Larson scores films for Todd Solondz and Lilya 4-ever.

eras.title: Two coasts, two drummers
eras.text: The reunion was loose by design: a hired guitarist and bassist, and a different drummer depending on which side of the country they were playing. It ended with a 2009 farewell at the Bowery Ballroom, then came back once more for the Black Cat's 20th birthday in 2013.

years.h: Shudder to Think reunite at the Mercury Lounge
years.p: Craig Wedren, Nathan Larson and Kevin March play their first Shudder to Think show in nearly a decade at New York's Mercury Lounge, with Mark Watrous on guitar and Jesse Krakow of Time of Orchids on bass.

years.h: Kevin March drums east, Adam Wade drums west
years.p: Shudder to Think's reunion keeps rolling. Kevin March drums the East Coast dates; Adam Wade comes back for the western ones, New Orleans included.

years.h: Reunion show at the 9:30 Club, October 10, 2008
yt: Reunion show at the 9:30 Club, October 10, 2008

years.h: Live from Home · Team Love
years.p: Shudder to Think's reunion shows, documented on a live album for Team Love.

years.h: Shudder to Think's farewell at the Bowery Ballroom
years.p: Shudder to Think play a goodbye show at the Bowery Ballroom in New York. Founding guitarist Chris Matthews joins them for the encore.

years.h: Shudder to Think play the Black Cat's 20th birthday
years.p: The Pony Express Record line-up of Craig Wedren, Nathan Larson, Adam Wade and Stuart Hill plays the D.C. club's anniversary, with Chris Matthews and Mike Russell joining for the encore.

eras.title: Back on Dischord, twenty-seven years on
eras.text: Craig Wedren survived a heart attack in 2018. Seven years later came something the reunions never offered: new songs, starting with Thirst Walk and Playback. And the band that left Dischord for a major put them out on Dischord.

years.h: Craig Wedren has a heart attack at 48
years.p: Craig Wedren has described paramedics carrying him out on a stretcher at 2 a.m. while his son watched. He told Vanyaland it left him with years of panic attacks, and a stronger will to live.

years.h: Shudder to Think play two surprise shows in Los Angeles
years.p: Craig Wedren, Nathan Larson and Adam Wade, with Clint Walsh on guitar and [[Jherek Bischoff|e0dcef88-0353-425c-99bd-81a36e96ed7f]] on bass, play Permanent Records Roadhouse as Shudder to Think and debut a new song, Playback.

years.h: Shudder to Think's Thirst Walk 7" · Dischord No. 201
years.p: Thirst Walk backed with Playback, Shudder to Think's first new music since the late 1990s. Dischord takes preorders on the label site and Bandcamp.

years.h: Shudder to Think's Who Sent You? EP
years.p: Three new Shudder to Think songs, released digitally the night the band plays Philadelphia. New York follows on September 12 and Los Angeles on September 20, with the Thirst Walk 7" repressed for the merch table.
